title: Ability-Easy Does It
coreMove: Shrink a stalled behavior to its smallest meaningful version by attacking whichever of time, money, physical effort, mental effort, routine fit, or social fit is the actual bottleneck

exampleSpecs.domain: a night-shift ICU nurse trying to start a stretching habit between 3am rounds
exampleSpecs.audience: a healthcare worker whose energy budget is already spent
exampleSpecs.stakes: chronic lower-back pain that will end her bedside career within five years if she does not move
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she identifies that mental effort, not time, is the bottleneck and cuts the habit from a ten-minute routine to a single hamstring stretch against the supply closet door

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance violist preparing for a regional audition while raising a toddler
exampleSpecs.audience: a working artist with fragmented practice time
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she keeps her chair in the orchestra or loses it to a younger player
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she opens the case and plays one bar — not as a warm-up, but as the entire practice — and feels the resistance dissolve the moment she lets the bar count

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional bakery owner trying to learn bookkeeping software after years of paper ledgers
exampleSpecs.audience: a small-business owner in his late fifties who has rejected three productivity systems
exampleSpecs.stakes: a tax season he cannot afford to botch again
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the before version asks him to reconcile a week of receipts on Sunday night; the after version is opening the app and tagging one transaction after he locks the front door

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school chemistry teacher and her partner negotiating who feeds the dog at 6am
exampleSpecs.audience: a couple where one person carries most of the household's invisible labor
exampleSpecs.stakes: a low-grade resentment that has started leaking into their weekends
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: they discover that the bottleneck is not willingness but routine fit — the partner's morning starts in a different room — and they redesign the cue around the coffee maker instead of the alarm

exampleSpecs.domain: a recently widowed retiree trying to walk daily after his cardiologist's warning
exampleSpecs.audience: an older reader for whom 'just thirty minutes a day' has been useless advice
exampleSpecs.stakes: a second cardiac event the doctor said was likely within eighteen months
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he sets the rule that the walk is putting on his shoes and stepping onto the porch — anything beyond that is optional — and on a hard grief day discovers that this is the only version he can actually do

exampleSpecs.domain: a junior immigration paralegal trying to drink more water during back-to-back client intakes
exampleSpecs.audience: a young professional in a high-volume desk job
exampleSpecs.stakes: recurring tension headaches that are starting to affect her case accuracy
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the reader is asked to predict which constraint is binding before the answer is revealed — it is not time or memory but the physical effort of standing up, solved by moving the bottle from the kitchen to her desk

exampleSpecs.domain: a divorced father re-learning to cook on the two nights a week his daughters stay over
exampleSpecs.audience: a parent stitching a household back together one routine at a time
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether his daughters experience these nights as a real home or a holding pattern
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he notices that the bottleneck was never skill or time but the mental load of choosing a recipe, and the tiny version becomes 'chop one onion before the kettle boils' — a behavior small enough to survive a bad week
